author: Augustine of Hippo
addressee: ordinary Christians, especially those attracted to or troubled by the Donatist party
occasion: Augustine composed a popular, singable psalm to persuade ordinary believers to remain in Catholic unity and to answer Donatist claims about the origins of their schism.
argument: Augustine urges those who rejoice in peace to judge the Donatist controversy truly. He retells the origin of the schism: Donatist leaders broke the net of the church by setting up altar against altar after failing to prove that Caecilian's ordainer had handed over the scriptures. He argues that the church is a mixed net of good and bad fish until the final separation at the shore, and that sinners must be tolerated within the church as Christ tolerated Judas. He appeals to the succession of bishops from Peter's see as the rock against which the gates of hell cannot prevail, and calls Donatists to return to the vine and to peace.

outline.move: The whole psalm addresses those who rejoice in peace, retells the Donatist schism, refutes Donatist claims, urges toleration of sinners within the church, and calls for return to catholic unity.

cast.name: Augustine
cast.who: The author and speaker of the psalm.

cast.name: Donatus
cast.who: Leader after whom the Donatist party is named; sought to control all Africa and rebaptized Christians.

cast.name: Caecilian
cast.who: Bishop of Carthage whose ordination the Donatist party rejected.

cast.name: Botrus
cast.who: Enemy of Caecilian involved in the original accusation.

cast.name: Caelestius
cast.who: Enemy of Caecilian involved in the original accusation.

cast.name: Macarius
cast.who: Imperial official associated with violence against Donatists; Donatists blamed Catholics for his actions.

cast.name: Judas
cast.who: The betrayer of Christ, used as an example of a tolerated sinner among the apostles.

cast.name: Peter
cast.who: Apostle whose see begins the succession of bishops identified as the rock of the church.

cast.name: John the Baptist
cast.who: Preacher who announced Christ's winnowing of the threshing floor.

cast.name: Ezekiel
cast.who: Prophet cited for those who groan over sins without separating.

voices.speaker: Augustine
voices.how_marked: The main voice of the psalm, speaking directly to the audience.

voices.speaker: Mother Church
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'ipsa mater ecclesia' speaking 'cum pace' to her children.

voices.speaker: A hypothetical catholic Christian
voices.how_marked: Introduced as 'Talis si quis ad te ueniat plenus catholica fide' and quoted as saying 'frater, quid me uis rebaptizare?'; the 'you' addressed is the Donatist interlocutor.

key_terms.sense: The net cast into the sea, representing the church gathering a mixed catch of good and bad.
A rival altar set up against the catholic altar, representing schism.
Those accused of handing over the scriptures during persecution.
The split or division caused by the Donatist party.
The unity of the catholic church, opposed to Donatist separation.
The peace of the church, broken by the Donatists.
The threshing floor, representing the church where wheat and chaff are mixed until the end.
Chaff, representing sinners within the church.
Wheat, representing the righteous within the church.
The episcopal seat, especially the see of Peter, representing legitimate authority.
The Donatist practice of baptizing again those who came from the catholic church.
Violent Donatist partisans associated with clubs and attacks.
The vine, representing Christ and the church, from which the Donatists are cut off.
The rock, identified with the succession of bishops from Peter's see, against which the gates of hell cannot prevail.

scripture: The author uses Old Latin or Vulgate forms and follows the Septuagint/Vulgate Psalm numbering. Cite Psalms by their modern Hebrew numbering where it differs, and use modern book names where the source uses older forms.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is approximate.
The precise identity of all named individuals such as Botrus and Caelestius is not fully established from the text alone.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Caelestius ... Enemy of Caecilian involved in the original accusation.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: erant Botrus et Caelestius hostes Caeciliano ualde, impii fures superbi, de quibus longum est referre. iunxerunt se simul omnes crimen in illum conflare, dicunt ordinatorem eius sanctos libros tradidisse.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Caelestius ... One of the enemies of Caecilian who joined in fabricating the charge that Caecilian's ordainer had handed over the holy books; called 'impious, thieving, proud'.

_unresolved_facts.claim: A hypothetical catholic Christian ... the 'you' addressed is the Donatist interlocutor.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Talis si quis ad te ueniat plenus catholica fide ... et si tibi dicat: 'frater, quid me uis rebaptizare?'
_unresolved_facts.fix: A hypothetical catholic Christian ... the 'you' (te/tibi) addressed is the Donatist party member or the Donatist side generally, not a specific interlocutor.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He appeals to the succession of bishops from Peter's see as the rock against which the gates of hell cannot prevail
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: numerate sacerdotes uel ab ipsa Petri sede et in ordine illo patrum quis cui successit uidete: ipsa est petra quam non uincunt superbae inferorum portae.
_unresolved_facts.fix: He appeals to counting the bishops from Peter's see itself and seeing who succeeded whom in that order of fathers; this succession itself is identified as the rock (petra), not Peter personally.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Donatist leaders broke the net of the church by setting up altar against altar after failing to prove that Caecilian's ordainer had handed over the scriptures
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: dicunt ordinatorem eius sanctos libros tradidisse. sic pacis retia ruperunt et errant modo per mare.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Donatist leaders broke the net of the church by setting up altar against altar; they claimed (falsely, per Augustine) that Caecilian's ordainer had handed over the holy books—the text presents this as their fabricated accusation, not as a failed proof.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He argues that the church is a mixed net of good and bad fish until the final separation at the shore
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: genus autem mixtum piscis iustus est cum peccatore; saeculi finis est litus: tunc est tempus separare
_unresolved_facts.fix: He argues that the mixed kind of fish is the just person with the sinner; the end of the age is the shore: then is the time to separate
